To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a-C(:H):H films have a high UV photodarkening efficiency, ΛUV,pdeff, which is a function of the hydrogen content, XH, of the film.
the a-C:H refractive index is dominated by the presence of hydrogen, and that a-C(:H):O and a-C(:H)-Si materials are optically similar.

a-C(:H):H materials are UV photodarkening, with photodarkening rates of 10-5 s-1 for the hydrogen-rich a-C(:H), and 10-6 s-1 for hydrogen-poor a-C(:H); and a-C(:H)-based materials are not UV photodarkened.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optical properties and photo-processing of amorphous hydrogenated carbon (a-C:H) films.
the optical properties and photoprocessing of hydrogen-rich amorphous carbons (a-C:H).
the evolution of the optical properties of hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C:H) films as a result of exposure to UV radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the photoprocessing time scales are shorter than the photodarkened material lifetimes, and that the photodarkness of a-C(:H), and its associated photodegradation, is a consequence of the photoprocessing.
the photodarkened a-C(:H)/a-C(:O) particles have an average photodarkening time-scale, τpd, ≃ 10−2 s, which is a factor ≃ 10 longer than that for the unprocessed particles.

the photodarkened state is a result of the photodissociation of H2 and H2O molecules, with the photodarkness being a result of the loss of the H2 molecules, which have a lower binding energy than H2O molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a-C(:H):H materials with a hydrogen concentration of XH < 0.23 (≡ Eg > 1.0 eV) are photostable in the 200-400 nm wavelength range and that the photodarkened a-C(:H:O:N) materials have photostable a-C(:H:N) core particles with a hydrogen concentration XH = 0.23.
the photodarkened a-C(:H):O materials are more stable than the original, as-prepared materials.
the a-C(:)H materials are highly photochemically reactive and, as a consequence, are not suitable for use as UV filters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, as a result of the photoprocessing, the refractive index of the hydrogen-rich a-C(:H)s increases, which is the basis of our photodarkening mechanism.
, in the absence of any other mechanism, a-C(:H):SiN x films are photostable on the time-scale of 1 yr, while a-C(:H)-based solar cells are expected to degrade on a similar timescale to a-C(:H).
a-C:H materials are very photostable, with a typical photoprocessing time for the a-C:H materials considered here of ~ 10 yr.
